lines.dialogue: No need to be defensive. It's not an attractive quality in a guru.

lines.scene: INT. SHELDON AND LEONARD'S APARTMENT - LATER (DAY 2)
lines.dialogue: Sim City. KOOTHRAPPALI You can't be in a video game. SHELDON Why not? I feel most at home in Sim City. But more specifically, the Sim City I designed, Sheldonopolis. KOOTHRAPPALI Okay, fine, you're in Sheldonopolis. SHELDON Where specifically? Sheldon Square? Sheldon Towers? Or Sheldon Stadium, home of the fighting Sheldons. KOOTHRAPPALI Whatever you like. SHELDON I thought this was supposed to be a guided meditation. KOOTHRAPPALI Fine, you're in Sheldon Square.

lines.scene: INT. MEN'S SECTION OF DEPARTMENT STORE - MOMENTS LATER
lines.dialogue: This is great. I had a suit like this when I was six.

lines.scene: INT. MEN'S SECTION OF DEPARTMENT STORE - MOMENTS LATER
lines.dialogue: This is ridiculous. I look like a clown. CUT TO:

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: That's how you start a psychotherapy session? "How am I doing?" I was promised a riverboat journey into the jungles of my subconscious. Instead I get the same question I hear from the lady who slices my bologna at Ralph's.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: Would it be helpful to you if I told you about my dreams?

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: I recently had a dream that I was a giant.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: But everything around me was to scale so it all looked normal. What do you make of that?

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: I was wearing size a million pants.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: Ahhh. The talking cure. Classical Freudian. Good choice. If it will help speed things along my answers to the standard Rorschach ink blot test are: A) a bat, B) a bat, C) a bat and D) my father killing my mother with a hypodermic needle.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: Really, Leonard? You're just going to try to recycle Adler's doctrine of the inferiority complex? I could probably get that from the woman at Ralph's and she'd let me taste some pieces of cheese for free.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: I see.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: Go on.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: I hear you saying you're angry with your mother.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: Thank you, Leonard.

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT (NIGHT 3)
lines.dialogue: If someone as damaged as you can find his way to crawl out of bed each morning, I think I can face a simple awards ceremony.

lines.scene: INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL - NIGHT (NIGHT 4)
lines.dialogue: I don't feel different. This alcohol is defective.

lines.scene: INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL - NIGHT (NIGHT 4)
lines.dialogue: All right, are you people ready to have some fun? Do you have a basic understanding of differential calculus and at least one year of algebraic topology? Then here come the jokes: Why did the chicken cross the Mobius strip? To get to the same side? Pow! A neutron walks into a bar and asks, "How much for a drink?" The bartender says, "For you, no charge." Hello? there. I can hear you metabolizing oxygen and expelling carbon dioxide.

lines.scene: INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL - NIGHT (NIGHT 4)
lines.dialogue: Looks like we have some academic dignitaries in the audience. Dr. Randall is here from the geology department, the only man who's happy when they take his work for granite.

lines.scene: INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL - NIGHT (NIGHT 4)
lines.dialogue: I kid the geologists of course, but that's only because I have no respect for the field. Let me ask you a question: Why are we all here? Because we're scientists. And what do scientists study? The universe. And what's the universe made of? Well, I'm glad you asked. (SINGING TOM LEHRER'S "THE ELEMENTS") THERE'S ANTIMONY, ARSENIC, ALUMINUM, SELENIUM / AND HYDROGEN AND OXYGEN AND NITROGEN AND RHENIUM / AND NICKEL, NEODYMIUM, NEPTUNIUM, GERMANIUM... (CALLING OUT TO CROWD) Everybody! (SINGING) AND IRON, AMERICIUM, RUTHENIUM, URANIUM, EUROPIUM, ZIRCONIUM, LUTETIUM, VANADIUM... (CALLING OUT TO CROWD) Just the Asians! SHELDON (CONT’D) AND ASTATINE AND RADIUM, AND GOLD AND

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT/INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL
lines.dialogue: Penny, Leonard. Would you be able to answer some questions I'm having about the events of last night?

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT/INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL
lines.dialogue: Question one: Where are my pants?

lines.scene: INT. LEONARD AND SHELDON'S APARTMENT/INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL
lines.dialogue: search?

lines.scene: INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL - NIGHT (NIGHT 4)
lines.dialogue: All right, people, let's get down to the math. It is only three dimensional thinking that limits our imagination. Can I take my pants off over my head? Of course not, my body's in the way.

lines.scene: INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL - NIGHT (NIGHT 4)
lines.dialogue: But if we had access to higher dimensions, we could move our pants around our bodies through the fourth dimension and our days of dropping trousers would be over!

lines.scene: INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL - NIGHT (NIGHT 4)
lines.dialogue: Oh Lord, how can this be any worse?

lines.scene: INT. AWARDS BANQUET HALL - NIGHT (NIGHT 4)
lines.dialogue: Now for the astronomers in the audience get ready to see the dark side of the moon. SHELDON (O.S.) (CONT’D) And here's Uranus. FADE OUT.
